draft.title: Improving sleep
card: Bright light therapy
exposure to bright light at set times, often with a light box. It can help reset the body clock, for example by shifting a late sleep time earlier.
Zeitgebers
cues from the environment that help set the body clock. Examples are daylight, temperature and meal times.
Sleep hygiene
habits that support good sleep. Examples are keeping regular sleep and wake times, avoiding screens and caffeine late in the day, and keeping the bedroom dark and quiet.
Light therapy and zeitgebers work on the body clock. Sleep hygiene works on daily habits and the sleep setting.
draft.remember: Reset the body clock with light and cues, and support sleep with good habits.

a.q: Which action is an example of sleep hygiene?
opts: Going to bed and waking at regular times
Using a light box at set times each morning
Using daylight to cue the body clock
Eating meals at set times to cue the body clock
a.why: Regular sleep and wake times are a habit that supports sleep, which is sleep hygiene. A light box is tempting, but that is bright light therapy, which works on the body clock.
a.clue: Which option is a daily habit rather than a light or environmental cue?

b.q: Priya's body clock runs late. Each morning she sits in bright light for 30 minutes, then walks outside. Why might this help?
opts: Light is a cue that helps reset her body clock earlier
Light is a sleep hygiene habit that makes her tired earlier
Light replaces the need for any sleep at night
Light lowers her body temperature so she sleeps longer
b.why: Bright light and daylight are cues that help reset the body clock, and morning light can shift it earlier. Calling it sleep hygiene is tempting, but sleep hygiene means habits and the sleep setting, not clock cues.
b.clue: Think about what light does to the body clock.

a.best: Going to bed and waking at regular times

b.best: Light is a cue that helps reset her body clock earlier

problems.detail: The last bullet splits the ideas too neatly: 'Light therapy and zeitgebers work on the body clock. Sleep hygiene works on daily habits.' Some sleep hygiene habits act on the body clock too. Regular sleep and wake times entrain it, and avoiding screens at night limits light that delays it. The Study Design stresses how zeitgebers and sleep hygiene interact, so this split could mislead.

The clue asks which option is 'a daily habit rather than a light or environmental cue'. Eating meals at set times is also a daily habit, so the clue does not cleanly separate the right option from that distractor.

proposal.title: Improving sleep
card: Bright light therapy
exposure to bright light at set times, often with a light box. Morning light can shift the body clock earlier, which helps a person whose sleep time runs late.
Zeitgebers
cues from the environment that help set the body clock. Examples are daylight, temperature and meal times.
Sleep hygiene
habits that support good sleep. Examples are keeping regular sleep and wake times, avoiding screens and caffeine late in the day, and keeping the bedroom dark and quiet.
These ideas overlap. Regular sleep and wake times help keep the body clock in step, and avoiding screens at night limits light that can delay it.
proposal.remember: Light and other cues can reset the body clock, and good sleep habits support sleep and help keep that clock steady.

a.q: Which action is an example of sleep hygiene?
opts: Keeping the bedroom dark and quiet at night
Sitting in front of a light box each morning
Drinking coffee in the evening to stay alert
Scrolling on a phone in bed to wind down
a.why: A dark, quiet bedroom is a habit that supports sleep, so it is sleep hygiene. A light box is tempting, but that is bright light therapy. Evening coffee and screens in bed work against good sleep.
a.clue: Which choice would make it easier to fall asleep?

b.q: Priya's body clock runs late. Each morning she sits in bright light for 30 minutes, then walks outside. Why might this help?
opts: Morning light is a cue that can shift her clock earlier
Morning light is a cue that can shift her clock later
Morning light can replace her need for sleep at night
Morning light can stop her body clock from working
b.why: Bright light and daylight are zeitgebers, and morning light can move the body clock earlier, so she gets sleepy sooner at night. Shifting it later is the tempting reversal, but that would make her late sleep time worse.
b.clue: Her clock runs late. Which way does it need to move?

a.best: Keeping the bedroom dark and quiet at night

b.best: Morning light is a cue that can shift her clock earlier
